Q. in the Ṛkprātiśākhya. Mu7nchen 30.
Sage Agastya figures a. a. interlocutor in several Purāṇas an. similar works a. a result of which portions of works narrated by him become current a. his works. The following is a list of some of the texts in which he is thus found a. a. interlocutor:
(a./i>) Vihagendrasaṁhitā. MD. 7510. 7520. TD. 15337 is wrong in ascribing the Vihagendrasaṁhitā itself to Agastya. In Pāñcarātra literature, the Vihagendra an. the Agastya are two different Saṁhitās. See enumeration of the Pāñcarātra texts in the Pādmatantra. IO. Eggeling p. 848b.
(b) Basavapurāṇa. MD. 2349.
(c) Devīpurāṇa. IO. 3362. [Page022-a.
(d) Agastya-Dilīpa-saṁvāda from the Skānda on the Māhātmya of Mylapore, Madras. Whish p.. 247-9.
(e) Lalitopākhyāna: “Brahmottarakhaṇḍe Hayagrīva-Agastya-saṁvāde Lalitopākhyāne”. MD. 2514. 9114. 9183. See printed text of the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa also for Agastya in the Lalitopākhyāna.
(f) Agastya-Śaunaka-saṁvāda. MD. 2582.
(g) Agastya-Nārada-saṁvāda in a work called Hiraṇyagarbhasaṁhitā in which occurs a. Rāmanavamīkalpa. MD. 8438.
(h) Agastya-Nārada-saṁvāda, 8 chs. on Gāyatrī. Taylor II. 251. See also PUL. II. App. p. 55, Gāyatrīviṣaya.
(i) Agastya-Vasu-saṁvāda in the Padmapurāṇa, Uparibhāga. MD. 15379.
(j) Agastya-Rāghava-saṁvāda containing the Śivagītā. MD. 9256.
(k) Skanda-Agastya-saṁvāda in the Kāśīkhaṇḍa of the Skānda.

Agastyapaṇḍita

On the basis of śl. 60 (p. 66. Bālamanoramā edn.) of the Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa, some scholars hold that Vidyānātha an. Agastya are identical. See J. Myth. Soc. X. p. 383. For a refutation of this theory, see J. Myth. Soc. XI. 1931. p. 286.
Agastyapaṇḍita is credited with 74 Kāvyas. Gaṅgādevī, pupil of Agastya's nephew, Viśvanātha, says in her Vīrakamparāyacarita--catussaptatikAvyoktivyaktavaiduSyasampade | agastyAya jagatyasmin spRhayet ko na kovidaH ||
